summary: Charles Taylor is a philosopher who studied at Selwyn House School, McGill University (~1948–1952), and Balliol College, Oxford (~1952–1961). He taught at McGill University (~1961–1997), Northwestern University (~2002), and the University of Montreal.

Charles Wei-hsun Fu was a scholar of philosophy, Buddhist studies, and sinology who studied at National Taiwan University (~1952–1956) and the University of Illinois System (~1965–1969). He held a post at Ohio University (~1968–1972).

Charles Wilkins was an Indologist and linguist who studied under Kālinātha (~1778–1786). He co-founded the Asiatic Society in 1784 and served as librarian for the East India Company and the India Office Library from the 1770s to 1836.

Charles-Joseph de Harlez de Deulin was a scholar of sinology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and Indology who earned a law doctorate at the University of Liège. He held posts at Collège Saint-Quirin and KU Leuven (~1871–1899).
Charlotte Furth was a scholar of sinology and history. She served as a professor at California State University (~1966–1989) and held a post at the University of Southern California (~1989–2008).

Chatral Sangye Dorje was a figure in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied under numerous teachers, including Ngawang Pelzang (~1928–1941), Dudjom Jigdral Yeshe Dorje—whom he later succeeded—Sera Khandro, and Dorje Dradül.

Chatsumarn Kabilsingh works in Buddhist studies and philosophy. She earned degrees from Visva-Bharati University, McMaster University, and Magadh University, and taught in Thammasat University's Department of Philosophy and Religion (~1973–2000).

Chen-kuo Lin is a scholar of philosophy and Buddhist studies who earned his doctorate from Temple University. He served as a professor and distinguished professor at National Chengchi University, with visiting positions at Leiden University and IIAS.
Cheng Huang has held academic posts at the University of Electronic Science and Technology of China, UT Southwestern Medical Center, and Southern Methodist University.
Cheng Yen is a religious figure in Buddhist and religious studies who studied as a disciple under Yinshun starting in 1963. She founded the Tzu Chi Foundation in 1966 and Tzu Chi University in 2000.
Cheryl A. Crowley is a Japanology scholar who studied under William R. LaFleur, Philip B. Yampolsky, Ryuichi Abe, and Barbara Ruch.
Chi Chen Ho is a scholar of Buddhist studies and sinology who studied under Hsuan Hua and Robert E. Buswell Jr., completing a PhD at UCLA in 2010, where Ho also served as a teaching assistant.
Chi-chiang Huang is a scholar of Buddhist studies, sinology, and history who completed a PhD at the University of Arizona in 1986 under Jing-shen Tao and also studied under Robert M. Gimello.

Chi-wah Chan works in sinology and Buddhist studies, earning a PhD from UCLA in 1993 under Robert E. Buswell Jr. and Benjamin A. Elman, and previously served as a teaching assistant at The Chinese University of Hong Kong.
Chie Ikeya is a historian who completed a PhD at Cornell University in 2006, studying under David K. Wyatt.
Chien Y. Hsu is a scholar of Buddhist studies who completed doctoral work under Leslie S. Kawamura and James B. Apple, and also studied under traditional teacher Zhenhua.
Chien-hsing Ho is a scholar of philosophy, Buddhist studies, and Indology. Ho has held posts at Nanhua University as an associate professor of religious studies and at Academia Sinica.
Chih-fu Li is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy who served as director of the Chung-Hwa Institute of Buddhist Studies.

Chih-mien Adrian Tseng is a scholar of Buddhist studies, religious studies, and sinology who earned a PhD at McMaster University under James A. Benn. Tseng has served on the faculty at Fo Guang University.

Chijo Akamatsu was a scholar of religious studies who studied at Kyoto University under Bunzaburo Matsumoto and at the University of Tokyo. He held professorships at Keijo Imperial, Koyasan, Hanazono, Ryukoku, and Yamaguchi universities.
